blocks.text: Main Street is also the line that splits the board's Mount Pleasant VE (east) and Mount Pleasant VW (west) sub-areas. Buildings below are counted only where a source places them on the corridor itself; Mount Pleasant VE product that a source places off-corridor is not imported.
The Independent (The Independent at Main) — 285 East 10th Avenue (also addressed 2508 Watson Street)

A project source records 258 condos in a 21-storey concrete tower, a residential/commercial/office mixed-use development by Rize Alliance at Main Street and East Broadway. Listings record year built 2019, Apartment/Condo, cats OK in the pet field; a building directory instead says the building was built in 2017 and states its strata bylaws include "Pets allowed, rentals allowed". Sources differ on the year built (2017 vs 2019).

A current listing records Subdivision Name "Cartier Place," Property Sub Type Apartment/Condo, Area Minor Mount Pleasant VE, year built 1991, and a pet field of cats OK; listing copy adds "Cats only, sorry no dogs!" and notes recent building upgrades.

Listings record Apartment/Condo units at this Main Street address in the board's "Main" sub-area, with construction recorded as frame wood / brick / concrete in one listing; a building source counts 90 properties at the address. Build year differs across listings — 2011 in several, 2012 in another.
Streets, schools and getting around Main

items.t: "Main" is a recognised smaller area of the city but not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas; the corridor runs through the Mount Pleasant, Riley Park and Sunset local areas.

Where condo stock actually concentrates: at the corridor's north end, around the Broadway / Kingsway / Main junction — the junction the City calls Mount Pleasant's commercial heart — where the stock is one concrete tower (The Independent, East 10th Avenue at Main) plus low-rise strata on Main Street itself further south (Cartier Place at East 20th Avenue's block, 3333 Main at East 20th–22nd). South of East King Edward Avenue the corridor's known apartment-condo stock thins out; the side streets are heritage and character houses, older walk-up rentals and newer low-rise product.

Cross streets and anchors: Main Street is crossed by Terminal Avenue, East Broadway, Kingsway, East King Edward Avenue, East 33rd Avenue, East 41st Avenue and East 49th Avenue. The Mount Pleasant Community Centre and library are at 1 Kingsway where Kingsway meets Main; the Sunset Community Centre sits on Main Street near East 49th Avenue; Guelph Park (2390 Brunswick Street, the "Dude Chilling Park") is one block east of Main.

Transit: route 8 runs via Main Street; the corridor is crossed by the 9 and 99 B-Line at East Broadway, the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, and the 49 at East 49th Avenue; the future Mount Pleasant Station (Broadway Subway) sits at Main Street and Broadway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Main

items.t: Area plan — the Broadway Plan: the Plan covers the corridor's north end (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues), was approved June 22, 2022 and updated in December 2024, and provides for buildings up to 20–30 storeys near the future Mount Pleasant Station, with renter protections and tenant relocation requirements that matter on any older rental-building purchase. The Plan is policy, not zoning — most sites still need rezoning. South of 16th Avenue the corridor runs on citywide direction from the Vancouver Official Development Plan (in force March 31, 2026).

The corridor's most famous "condo" building cannot be mortgaged. The Lee Building (1912) sells as undivided interest under a tenants-in-common agreement dating to late 1993 — its listings say "cannot be financed" in plain words — so its prices are not comparables for strata product at The Independent two blocks away.

The Independent carries two addresses. It is marketed as 285 East 10th Avenue and also addressed 2508 Watson Street — documents, parking and storage records may use either, so match by strata lot, not by address alone.

"Main" is three products wearing one name. The Broadway / Kingsway station blocks, the South Main retail blocks around Cartier Place and 3333 Main, and the quieter Riley Park side streets south of King Edward price off different drivers — Broadway Plan expectations at the north end, R1-1 multiplex math on the side streets.

The corridor's civic anchor sits exactly on the corridor. The Mount Pleasant Community Centre and library at 1 Kingsway (opened December 2009, roughly 30,000 sq ft, LEED Gold, co-located with rental housing) is where Kingsway meets Main — the amenity base for The Independent and the north-end low-rises.

Cartier Place's pet rule is cats-only, in the listing's own words. "Cats only, sorry no dogs!" — a bylaw-style restriction that survives the 2022 rental-bylaw change, because pet bylaws were never voided. A dog owner should treat Cartier Place as a no until the registered bylaws say otherwise.

The north end's flood question is real and the south end's is not. The designated floodplain reaches the corridor only at the former False Creek shoreline lowland by Terminal Avenue; the grid south of 2nd Avenue sits on the Mount Pleasant slope.

blocks.text: Main Street is also the line that splits the board's Mount Pleasant VE (east) and Mount Pleasant VW (west) sub-areas.
E15 Just Off Main (OpenForm Properties) — 322 East 15th Avenue, at Sophia Street.

The developer's own project coverage describes a 49-unit residential project comprising both townhomes and one-level residences at East 15th Avenue and Sophia Street, with three-level townhomes with three bedrooms, dens and rooftop decks, and homes ranging from 450 to more than 1,400 sq ft; a trade source calls it a townhouse development of 49 townhouses including studios and one-, two- and three-bedroom units, on the former Bethlehem Lutheran Church site. A presale source instead records four 4-storey low-rise blocks and 51 strata homes described as garden flats plus stacked townhomes, and states the project is move-in ready; the developer's site states it is sold out to its 49 buyers. Tenure evidence: the presale source's "strata homes" description and the developer's strata-fee incentive — strata, not fee-simple. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: confirm on the Form B.

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: on the side streets just off Main, not on the Main Street frontage itself. South of East King Edward Avenue the corridor's known attached stock thins out to heritage and character houses and newer low-rise product on the side streets.

items.t: Form B diligence (E15, the one counted strata complex): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. The Lee Building exclusion in shows the limit of this protection: an undivided-interest building has no Form B at all, so the absence of one is itself the first diligence answer.

Plan — the Broadway Plan: the Plan covers the corridor's north end (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues), was approved June 22, 2022 and updated in December 2024, and provides for buildings up to 20–30 storeys near the future Mount Pleasant Station, with renter protections and tenant relocation requirements that matter on any older rental-building purchase. The Plan is policy, not zoning — most sites still need rezoning. South of 16th Avenue the corridor runs on citywide direction from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

The corridor's one townhouse complex stands on a church site. E15 was built on the former Bethlehem Lutheran Church site at East 15th Avenue and Sophia Street, in four low-rise blocks around a shared landscaped courtyard, with unit exteriors carrying custom murals by a Vancouver artist — the form is courtyard townhomes and garden flats, not a Main Street frontage building.
A named townhouse complex behind a Main Street condo building rests on one directory alone.

Side-street house lots: heritage and character detached houses on the side streets, much of them converted or suited, sit freehold; older walk-up rental apartments run along Main Street, Kingsway and Broadway, with newer low-rise and mid-rise strata condos and purpose-built rentals near Main Street and Kingsway.

Lot character from the zone, as stated: the residential side streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m), 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size.
Serviced position: corridor homes are on City water and sewer services.

Flood position: the corridor's north end touches the former False Creek shoreline lowland at Great Northern Way / Terminal, where the City's designated floodplain includes the False Creek coastal floodplain and parcels are subject to the Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements; the residential grid south of 2nd Avenue sits on the Mount Pleasant slope.

Historic fabric — built lots, not offerings: the area high above False Creek was named "Mount Pleasant" in 1888, and the City emphasises its heritage buildings, with the corridor's signature stock dated to the early 1900s in the Mount Pleasant Historic Context Statement. That heritage layer is diligence context for side-street lots, not a land offering.

The Lee Building — 151–189 East Broadway (listings use 175 East Broadway), at Main Street.: The seven-storey landmark the City's Mount Pleasant Historic Context Statement calls the area's signature heritage building, built 1911–1912 and listed on the City of Vancouver Heritage Register. Current listings state expressly that the property is Undivided Interest (Title to Land: Undivided Interest), that it "cannot be financed" and is a cash purchase only, owned under a tenants-in-common agreement, with no strata Form B regime.

Broadway Plan area (corridor north end): the Broadway Plan, approved June 22, 2022, is a 30-year framework (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues) providing for buildings up to 20–30 storeys near the future Mount Pleasant Station, with Council-approved updates in December 2024. Most sites still need rezoning — plan expectation is not entitled density, and no parcel in the plan area is presented here as a for-sale development site.
The Independent, 285 East 10th Avenue
New development: the Broadway Subway station build at Main and Broadway is the corridor's major project.

items.t: "Main" is the Main Street corridor in Vancouver East: the retail and residential spine running south from False Creek / Terminal Avenue through Mount Pleasant and Riley Park toward the Sunset local area at East 49th Avenue. The City lists "Main" as a recognised smaller area, but Main is not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas — the corridor runs through the Mount Pleasant, Riley Park and Sunset local areas.
Nearby areas: Mount Pleasant VW across Main Street to the west at the north end, Strathcona and Grandview-Woodland to the north-east, Kensington-Cedar Cottage to the east, Sunset to the south.

Main roads: Main Street is crossed by Terminal Avenue, East Broadway, Kingsway, East King Edward Avenue, East 33rd Avenue, East 41st Avenue and East 49th Avenue; the corridor's commercial heart is where Broadway, Kingsway and Main Street meet. Transit: route 8 runs via Main Street, crossed by the 9 and 99 B-Line at East Broadway, the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, and the 49 at East 49th Avenue; the future Mount Pleasant Station (Broadway Subway) sits at Main Street and Broadway, scheduled to open in fall 2027.

Civic anchors: Mount Pleasant Community Centre and the Mount Pleasant Branch library are at 1 Kingsway, where Kingsway meets Main Street; Sunset Community Centre is on Main Street near East 49th Avenue. Mount Saint Joseph Hospital (Prince Edward Street entrance) is just east of the corridor; Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is west of the corridor.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Main

items.t: Plans — Broadway Plan + Vancouver Official Development Plan: the Broadway Plan (approved June 22, 2022; updates December 2024) covers the corridor's north end and supports buildings up to 20–30 storeys near Mount Pleasant Station; the Vancouver Plan (approved July 22, 2022) was rescinded and replaced by the Vancouver Official Development Plan on March 31, 2026.

Heritage / renter diligence at the north end: for older Main Street rental buildings, the Broadway Plan's renter protections and tenant relocation requirements must be factored in before underwriting a redevelopment purchase, and Mount Pleasant's heritage-retention expectations affect the side-street stock the context statement documents.

Floodplain diligence: the designated floodplain includes the False Creek coastal floodplain at the corridor's north end, with Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements for parcels in it — confirm the specific parcel in the City dataset.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Main corridor ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.
Comping across all three at once misprices every one of them.

"Dude Chilling Park" is an official park fact: Guelph Park, 2390 Brunswick Street, one block east of Main Street in Mount Pleasant, is the park known by its adopted "Dude Chilling Park" sign, with tennis courts, a playground and the Brewery Creek Community Garden.

The civic building at 1 Kingsway is three things at once (opened December 2009): the roughly 30,000 sq ft Mount Pleasant Community Centre, the VPL Mount Pleasant Branch and City rental housing are co-located in one LEED Gold building where Kingsway meets Main.

The plan layer changed on March 31, 2026: the Vancouver Plan was rescinded and replaced by the Vancouver Official Development Plan on that date — older page copy citing the Vancouver Plan as current is dated.

faq.q: Is Main a Vancouver West or Vancouver East area?

faq.q: What condo stock does the corridor actually have?

faq.a: Tenure. Listings state it is undivided interest under a tenants-in-common agreement, that it cannot be financed (cash purchase only), and that taxes are bundled into the monthly fee rather than paid on a strata lot. There is no strata corporation, no Form B and no CMHC-insured mortgage route.
faq.q: The Lee Building looks cheap for its size and location — what is the catch?
